- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment: if sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model often over-optimistic; cap forecast at +5% above recent 14-day moving average.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (especially in 10–15 day horizon), apply a “sentiment-adjusted downward bias” — reduce forecast by 1–3% per 0.10 sentiment drop.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 14-day smoothed average as anchor for correction.
